title: Realize the sparse correction as a reversible nearest-grid map
body:
The actual 74-ADD correction from PR6537 now has a nearest-grid data implementation with an exact inverse and no retained rounding transcript. Round each source product before its in-place ADD. Every output is a nearest grid point to the exact correction in both directions; the sharp error is `h/2` per real coordinate. A half-integer output proves the uniform lower bound.

The fractional-error amplification falls from 21 for the old 569-gate forward block to 1 for the new block. Its inverse also has factor 1. All 44 minimum-cost source candidates attain the same bound, so the published program already suffices. The original rank-two construction, 74 gates and scalar allowance remain credited to PR6537; no new cost optimum or kappa is claimed.

For fields with D complex coordinates and incoming field error eta, the resulting correction-boundary contract is `15 eta + h sqrt(D/2)`. A signed range strictly above `84A` suffices when integer input components are bounded by A. Integer arithmetic is exact apart from the 25 source-product quantizations. A backend that perturbs all operations must use the separately retained larger budgets. The exact-arithmetic allowance is not reused as an unproved rounded tape tariff.

Evidence: two exact transfer engines agree on all output coefficients and every prefix bound; attaining error witnesses are retained. A proved two-form periodicity reduces all integer rounding behavior to 64 classes per direction. All 128 classes, 40 large signed cases, 3,081 quantizer cases and six controls pass. A full-program control shows that rounding the whole accumulator instead fails to restore thirteen fields. Normal/optimized registered CPython 3.12, committed bytes/modes, official 16-file export with six inputs, read-only Git-free empty-PATH replay and source-corruption rejection pass. Optional full-history verification was not run in the shallow checkout. Hosted CI is separate.

Scope: exact restoration of the data fields and nearest-grid correction behavior. Reversible Boolean arithmetic, physical auxiliary cleanup, raw native entry errors, full caller/compiler/outer admission and all five framework assumptions remain open. No selected record changes.

Reproduce: `python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/rounded-sparse-correction`.

Fresh canonical main `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priority 8, selected PR6030. Overlap covered 489 open PRs and 6,481 Discussion records; live handoffs and recent PRs were rechecked before submission. [Scoped claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5645#discussioncomment-19365965). PR6540's native coarsening/residue codec is a different interface.

Prepared by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit PR6537, PR6529, Rohan Arun / PR6399, Erwan L. / PR6453, DreamingOfClouds, Cinna Davis, David Arias, Gareth Davidson, Jacob Alan Sussman, zxv, Cao Yifan and the retained source authors. Exact source inputs and original notices remain. Reversible integer lifting, nearest-even rounding and linear error propagation are classical. Apache-2.0.
